titulo: The four cases: nominativo, acusativo, dativo e genitivo: What a case is

aula.titulo: The four cases: nominativo, acusativo, dativo e genitivo
aula.objetivo: Understand what the four cases of German are (Nominativ, Akkusativ, Dativ, Genitiv), read the complete table of articles and use the personal pronouns in the nominative, accusative and dative.

blocos.explicacao: In German the function of a word in the sentence appears in the ARTICLE (and in some endings). There are four cases. NOMINATIVE: who does the action, the subject (wer? was?). AKKUSATIV: the direct object (wen? was?). DATIV: the indirect object, the one to whom something is given, said or helped (wem?). GENITIV: possession (wessen?). In «Der Mann gibt dem Kind einen Apfel»: «der Mann» is the subject (nominative), «dem Kind» is the one he gives to (dative) and «einen Apfel» is what he gives (accusative). You already use the nominative and the accusative; in this lesson the complete table begins.
blocos.comparacao: In English the function shows in the word order and in prepositions («give the apple to the boy»). In German it shows in the article: «dem Kind» already says «to the child».

tabela.question: wessen?
tabela.example: Das ist das Auto des Mannes.

erros.motivo: The masculine direct object goes into the accusative.

blocos.enunciado: Diga: «Der Mann liest. Ich sehe den Mann. Ich helfe dem Mann. Das ist das Auto des Mannes.»
